rules.R1: Lexical finite signatures only; unknown whole never supplies an entity.
rules.R2: MaterialSchema + MaterialProperty -> qualified MaterialSchema, left head and right property; fused and split nominal construction identical.
rules.R3: p(MaterialSchema) introduces fresh described Material, sets TOPIC and CURRENT. Applies generically at any written position; no singleton name or paragraph macro.
rules.R4: sh(ContainerSchema) introduces C and Contains(C,CURRENT), requiring a previously bound Material; does not replace CURRENT Material.
rules.R5: q(NominalExpr Material) evaluates explicit policy context and introduces fresh proper portion of it; sets CURRENT. This is a complete nominal expression, not an event expression.
rules.R6: s(NominalExpr Material) subdivides explicit input, addressing a fresh working Material part; sets CURRENT.
rules.R7: o(MaterialProperty) makes dispersed-property nominal expression evaluated against explicit context; no Event/Motion domain.
rules.R8: d(MaterialSchema/property) adds dense property; no independent introduction.
rules.R9: Bare nominal/property evaluates explicit context and asserts its paid properties; no ambient Material or Container.
rules.R10: NominalExpr + Event(Material) supplies explicit patient by nominal context evaluation, in fused or separate spelling; no event-to-material cast.

defaults.D1: Unexpressed Material event patient is explicit policy context TOPIC or CURRENT only.
defaults.D2: Maceration/drying preserves input; CHEDY explicitly creates a retained part and updates CURRENT.
defaults.D3: Bare property modifies selected context, not a fresh independent object.
defaults.D4: Unknown contribution invalidates TOPIC/CURRENT/OWNER continuity; no crossing. Fresh p schema may start local derivation, never consumes prior unknowns.

policies.TOPIC: Context argument is latest p-introduced Material; q/s/CHEDY do not replace it.
policies.CURRENT: Context argument is latest derived Material; q/s/CHEDY update it.

f85: SHEODY MaterialSchema -> d adds dense property -> p introduces M1 by R3. TOPIC=CURRENT=M1.
DOL ContainerSchema -> sh introduces C1 with Contains(C1,M1), requires written M1; no hidden owner.
SHEY Event(Material) -> macerate M1 under both policies, identity preserved.
f80: OL MaterialSchema -> p introduces M2; TOPIC=CURRENT=M2; no Container introduced.
OL+KAIN qualified mixture schema evaluates M2 and asserts grain-bearing.
OCKHY paid powdered property of M2.
o(KAIIN) dispersed powder-fine nominal expression; q creates proper portion P5 from M2 and sets CURRENT=P5, TOPIC=M2.
o(KAIN) qualifies selected M2 or P5 as dispersed grain-bearing.
o(KAR) qualifies selected M2 or P5 as dense dispersed.
SHEY uses M2 under TOPIC versus P5 under CURRENT: same actual maceration predicate, different written input identity.
